subject.title: Reject unsupported diagnostics OTel grpc config

question: Should OpenClaw remove `diagnostics.otel.protocol: "grpc"` from canonical config now, with this doctor migration as the upgrade path, or preserve the config value until real gRPC exporter support exists?
rationale: The code shape is reviewable, but removing a shipped config enum value and disabling enabled telemetry during repair is an operator-facing compatibility decision that automation should not make on behalf of maintainers.

options.title: Accept narrow rejection with doctor repair
options.body: Merge this PR shape so canonical config only accepts `http/protobuf`, and doctor removes legacy `grpc` while preserving the prior no-export outcome for active OTLP signals.

options.title: Pause for real gRPC exporter support
options.body: Keep `grpc` as a config value only if maintainers want to add actual gRPC exporters, package/dependency coverage, docs, and end-to-end tests instead of rejecting it.

options.title: Keep current warning-only runtime behavior
options.body: Leave validation accepting `grpc` and rely on runtime warnings, accepting the existing observability foot-gun reported by the linked issue.

recommendation.title: Accept narrow rejection with doctor repair
recommendation.body: Merge this PR shape so canonical config only accepts `http/protobuf`, and doctor removes legacy `grpc` while preserving the prior no-export outcome for active OTLP signals.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the diagnostics OTel service/config surface and also touched the runtime legacy migration area, making them the best available routing owner for the compatibility decision.
